To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the island of stability of superheavy nuclei around Z = 114 and N = 184 persists for the excited states of superheavy nuclei, and the island of stability is determined by the nuclear structure effect.

the survival probabilities of excited superheavy nuclides against neutron emission and neutron-induced fission are systematically investigated and the island of stability of superheavy nuclids around Z = 114-116 and N = 178-180 predicted in our previous work persists in the sense that it shows up in the survival probabilities of these superheavy nuclid.
the survival probability against neutron emission and the fission of excited SHN is maximized around Z=115 and N =179.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the survival probabilities in the fission channel and neutron emission channel of excited SHN, the optimal excitation energies for the survival probabilities, and their dependence on the neutron separation energy and the shell correction energy.
the stability of excited SHN against fission in their 1n-channel.
the survival probability of excited SHN against fission.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there exists an island of stability around Z = 114–116 and N = 180–182 for both the ground and excited states of SHN.
the island of stability of the ground states of SHN around the Z = 115, N = 179 is maintained for their first excited states.

the survival probability against neutron emission and/or fission in the ground state and excited states of SHN is mainly determined by their neutron separation energies and the shell correction energies, respectively, in the sense that a SHN is more likely to survive against neutron emission and/ or fission if its neutron separation energy is larger and its shell correction energy is larger, respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the island of stability of excited SHN predicted in this work is mainly due to the nuclear shell effect.
the nuclear shell effects play an important role in determining the stability of excited SHN in both the 1n- and 2n-channels.

the nuclear shell effects are dominant for the survival probability in both the 1n and 2n channels of SHN, whereas the nuclear shell effects and the nuclear deformation effects are comparable for the survival probability of the 1n channel of SHN.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the shell correction energies are crucial for the survival probability in fission.
the survival probability against 1n-fission of excited SHN is maximized around Z=115 and N=179.
it is important to take account of the shell effect in the study of the stability of excited SHN.
